items.title: ServerOS: A Self-Hosted Control Panel for Managing Your Linux Servers
items.summary: Managing several Linux servers often means juggling SSH sessions, deployment scripts, monitoring tools, and backups across different providers. While those tools get the job done, keeping everything organized becomes more complicated as your infrastructure grows. ServerOS takes a different approach by providing a centralized web interface for managing servers you already own. Rather than moving your infrastructure to another hosting platform, you connect your existing machines and manage applications, deployments, monitoring, and maintenance from one place.

items.title: OpenPost Combines Social Media Scheduling, Content Creation, and Automation in One Self-Hosted App

items.title: FAA Makes Helicopter Separation Ban Permanent
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is making permanent a restriction on how air traffic controllers handle helicopters crossing paths with arriving and departing aircraft in busy airspace. Two FAA notices issued Nov. 24 update air traffic control procedures and take effect Dec. 24. The first notice, JO 7110.808, makes permanent an interim restriction introduced in March. It prohibits controllers from using visual separation when a helicopter or powered-lift aircraft crosses the path of arriving or departing traffic in Class B, Class C or Terminal Radar Service Area (TRSA) airspace.

items.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon

items.title: Intel Xe Driver Gaining PCIe Function Level Reset "FLR" With Linux 7.5
items.summary: Last week's drm-xe-next pull request of new Xe kernel driver material that Intel has ready for Linux 7.5 finally introduces PCIe Function Level Reset (FLR) support for this modern Intel graphics driver. PCIe Function Level Reset is a standardized mechanism for resetting individual PCIe functions without impacting other functions on the same device or other PCIe devices on the system. PCIe FLR can be useful for virtualization and SR-IOV as well as targeted error recovery. Linux itself has supported PCIe FLR for years but now it's a matter of the Intel Xe driver finally supporting it.

items.title: Six Killed In Cessna 210 Crash Off Mississippi Coast
items.summary: A Cessna 210 crashed off the Mississippi coast Tuesday afternoon, killing all six people aboard. The aircraft went down approximately two miles northeast of Horn Island, between Pascagoula, Mississippi, and the island, according to the U.S. Coast Guard. Four adults and two boys, ages 8 and 10, were aboard. The Mobile, Alabama, air traffic control tower notified the Coast Guard at approximately 3:45 p.m. local time Tuesday after losing communication with the aircraft.

items.title: FAA Restores Touch-and-Goes at Centennial Airport

items.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus

items.title: Verifiable Social Reasoning for LLM Assistants

items.summary: The astronauts on the International Space Station will celebrate Thanksgiving with some nontraditional fare. Well, NASA astronaut Anil Menon will, anyway. In a video the agency released on Monday (Nov. 23), Menon showed off some of the plants he and his crewmates are growing in orbit and told us what's in store for the greens. "We need plants to survive as we set up our moon base, and as we go to Mars, we're going to have to grow our own nutrition. So that's what we're doing this Thanksgiving," Menon said in the 2.5-minute video.

items.title: Euclid's Record-Setting Quasar Probes Black Hole Formation
items.summary: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has found a record-setting quasar. Euclid found it at redshift z=8.13, corresponding to about 630 million years after the Big Bang. It beats the record by about 40 million years. How these quasars formed is puzzling, but each new detection at greater distances leads incrementally toward an answer.

items.title: A home NAS doesn't need 10GbE, these are the 3 things I'd spend that money on first
items.summary: Upgrading a NAS with 10-gigabit Ethernet requires matching hardware across the entire data path, from switches, network cards or adapters, cabling or transceivers, and client endpoints, which quickly drives up cost and power draw. In practical home workloads such as media streaming, routine backups, container hosting, and multi-drive hard disk drive arrays, mechanical drive speeds, protocol overhead, encryption, or client interfaces frequently cap throughput well below 10Gbps even when a 10GbE link is present.

items.title: Study Finds Artemis Astronauts Will Enjoy Moon-Grown Potatoes
items.summary: This is good news for space agencies like NASA that are actively planning to send astronauts back to the Moon, and this time, to stay. Through the Artemis Program, crews will land around the South Pole-Aitken Basin and begin constructing a permanent base that will enable regular missions in the future (about one per year). China's National Space Agency (CNSA) and Roscosmos also plan on building a base - the International Lunar Research Station (ILRS) - in the same region by the end of the decade.

items.title: FAA Seeks Information On Unexpected Stall Behavior In Piper Seminoles
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating a reported stall characteristic in Piper PA-44 Seminole aircraft after an airplane rolled 60 degrees or more during a wings-level stall maneuver. In an Airworthiness Concerns Sheet issued Nov. 24, the FAA said it was notified of an event in which the aircraft experienced a significant roll accompanied by a pitch-down and yaw at the stall. Similar behavior was observed with flap settings ranging from zero to 40 degrees. The event occurred with three people aboard, and the FAA said the behavior may be more likely under that configuration.

items.title: Ubuntu details plans to ‘replace’ its app grid with an AI smart launcher
items.summary: Canonical has shared more detail on plans for an AI-powered Ubuntu launcher, which it hopes will offer users “a new way to interact” with the desktop. In a post on Ubuntu Discourse, Canonical desktop engineer Didier Roche says the goal is to create a unified ‘entry point’ that lets users open apps and find files, but also access AI features when they explicitly want it. This will go beyond providing an alternative to the app grid, allowing for ‘prompt’ style workflows that use privacy-friendly AI models that run locally.

items.title: 34-Year-Old FedEx MD-11 Runs Off Miami Runway, Triggering Major FAA Ground Stop
items.summary: MIAMI – A 34-year-old McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighter operated by FedEx Express (FX) overshot the runway at Miami,Florida, after landing at Miami International Airport (MIA) on Wednesday, November 25. The incident prompted the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to impose a ground stop, disrupting flight operations during one of the busiest travel periods of the year in the United States. The aircraft was operating as FedEx Flight 910 from Memphis International Airport (MEM) to Miami. Although the runway excursion triggered an emergency response and temporary runway restrictions, authorities reported no injuries among the crew.

items.title: The Event Horizon Telescope Views the Dynamics and Geometry of a Black Hole Jet in Extreme Detail
items.summary: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), a massive international collaboration of scientists and radio observatories, is like the gift that keeps on giving. In 2019, the EHT Collaboration gave us the first image of a black hole: the supermassive black hole (SMBH) at the heart of the M87 galaxy (M87*). In 2022, it provided the first image of Sagittarius A*, the SMBH at the center of the Milky Way. Between 2024 and 2026, the international array also produced detailed images of the relativistic jet emanating from 3C 84 and M87*.

items.title: Arizona acrobats freed after weeks in ICE detention
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — Two Arizona acrobats who were detained by immigration agents at Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport have been released after weeks in custody. Agustin Baccega and his husband Gustavo Romanello were reunited Wednesday night for the first time since their detention. They are originally from Argentina and spent years with Arizona Circus Center in Tempe. Agents stopped them at Phoenix Sky Harbor as they were coming back to attend a memorial for a fellow circus trainer. Close friends told Arizona’s Family the couple had moved to Florida and had just walked off a plane in Phoenix, where Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents were waiting for them.

items.title: F2FS Getting Ready With Its Large Folios Support
items.summary: In recent months there has been a lot of work done by developer Nanzhe Zhao on implementing support for large folios for most readable/writable files with the F2FS file-system in its buffered I/O paths. This can bring some performance benefits and it's looking like the work may be wrapped up in time for the Linux 7.5 kernel…

items.title: Love and Murder in Medieval Cyprus: Pierre I and Joanna l’Aleman
items.summary: The love affair between King Pierre I and Joanna l’Aleman unfolded amid court intrigue, imprisonment and assassination in medieval Cyprus. Nicholas Costa explores their tragic story through a medieval chronicle, the ballad of Arodafnousa and clues preserved in the landscape of western Cyprus. This work examines the love affair between King Pierre I Lusignan of Cyprus and his courtier Joanna l’Aleman. The primary source is Leontios Macheras’s Recital concerning the sweet land of Cyprus entitled ‘Chronicle’, written in Cypriot Greek between 1426 and 1432, roughly fifty to sixty years after the events.

items.title: Anthropic chief denies wanting humans to 'surrender' free will to AI
items.summary: Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei on Wednesday denied wanting humanity to give up its free will to AI, calling it "absurd" to attribute the idea to him as rival tech leaders push back.

items.title: Open-weight models are the hottest thing in AI. Are they right for you?
items.summary: For the first three years of the generative artificial intelligence boom, enterprise technology strategy relied on a simple rule: Select the premier frontier foundation model, route every prompt through its commercial application programming interface and pay the subscription premium for access to cutting-edge technology. That monolithic approach is now collapsing under the weight of operational…

items.title: AI soccer talent app heading to Europe
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is making its way onto the soccer field through an app designed to identify young talent, which is set for its European launch in January.

items.title: Robots roam Singapore's urban AI testing ground
items.summary: When coffee is spilled at an office block in a futuristic enclave of Singapore, AI-powered cameras and sensors detect it and send a cleaning robot right away.

items.title: Jews in Medieval France: Between Tolerance and Persecution
items.summary: Jewish communities in medieval France experienced periods of coexistence alongside restrictive laws, forced conversions and brutal persecution. Lucie Laumonier traces how religious prejudice, royal policies and crises such as the Crusades and the Black Death shaped their lives. Judaism predates Christianity, but early Christians held ambivalent attitudes toward their Jewish cousins. The Council of Nicaea, held in 325, officially accused the Jews of having caused the death of Jesus Christ. Perceived as a “God-killing race” by Christians, the Jewish community usually faced hostility in Christian territories – that is, in most of Western Europe.

items.title: Claude artifacts can now be installed as desktop apps (just not on Linux)
items.summary: Claude now lets users install artifacts, small interactive tools the LLM can create inside of chats, as standalone(ish) desktop apps. When added via the ‘Install as app’, artifacts run in their own window with their own icon. They can also send desktop notifications, register keyboard shortcuts and add applets to the panel. Full system permissions can be granted, letting apps read, edit and delete files. The new feature is in beta but available to users on all plans, including free tiers, in the latest version of the Claude desktop apps for Windows and macOS (as of 24 November 2026).

items.title: Red-eye flight diverted to Sky Harbor after passenger tried to tamper with exit door
items.summary: A Chicago-bound American Airlines red-eye flight was diverted to Phoenix early Wednesday after a passenger tried to tamper with an exit door, police said. Crew members and passengers restrained the man until Flight 1494, which had departed from San Diego, landed safely at Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport about 1 a.m. Phoenix police said preliminary information shows the man got up, moved to the front of the plane and repeatedly refused crew instructions to return to his seat before going for the door.

items.summary: Artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc. launched today with $100 million in funding. items.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
items.summary: The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac. December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon)..

items.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
items.summary: On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes.

items.title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
items.summary: Two of NASA's four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks. The missions affected by the outages — hopefully temporary — are NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water.

items.title: Linux 7.4 Disables LLVM Profi Usage To Avoid Performance Hit, Pathological Build Times
items.summary: A change merged this week to the Linux 7.4 kernel and also set to be back-ported to stable kernel branches is to disable use of LLVM's Profi flow-based profile inference algorithm when leveraging AutoFDO. LLVM's Profi is a flow-based profile inference algorithm designed to address inaccuracies and other issues during profile guided optimizations (PGO) by the compiler. Profi has been in use by default since Clang 21 when the "-fprofile-sample-use" argument is passed. Unfortunately, this ended up causing problems for the Linux kernel builds that are built with LLVM/Clang and with AutoFDO being used for the automatic feedback directed optimizations.

items.summary: Interviews with 17 scientists reveal what they want to verify, safeguard, and keep under human control when using AI agents in research.

items.summary: More than 417,000 flights will operate in the U.S. this week and early next week as Americans travel ahead of and after Thanksgiving, according to the FAA. items.title: "Europe's largest museum development" opens in 1930s Citroën garage in Brussels
items.summary: Brussels ' former Citroën Garage has been transformed into Kanal, a 40,000-square-metre museum for modern art and architecture with an exhibition programme developed with the Parisian art institution Centre Pompidou. The transformation was designed by Atelier Kanal, a consortium made up of architecture studio EM2N, NoAarchitecten and Sergison Bates Architects, with a team of construction workers, who restored the 1930s industrial building and added three new volumes within its structure.

items.title: Meet BC Architects & Studies & Materials, Marina Tabassum's pick for the most influential architect of the next 20 years
items.summary: In this interview for Dezeen’s 20×20 project in partnership with Kohler, two of BC Architects & Studies & Materials’ founders discuss how their ideas have gone from being perceived as the product of “young idealism” to being taken seriously by the construction sector. The Brussels-based studio is at the forefront of bio-regional and circular design, with a whole arm of its practice dedicated to the development of new materials, often making use of construction waste.

items.title: RSHP centres cantilevered office building Sąvaržėlė around glass atrium
items.summary: UK studio RHSP has revealed its first project in the Baltic region, a mixed-use office building in Lithuania designed as "a landmark that is unmistakably forward-looking". Named after the Lithuanian word for paperclip, the seven-storey Sąvaržėlė is located in central Vilnius, between the UNESCO-listed Old Town and the city's commercial district. The stacked building has a cantilevered design and houses office space, a conference hall, a restaurant and a cafe across its 19,000-square-metre space.

items.title: Carlo Ratti and AI assistant to curate Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism 2027
items.summary: Italian architect Carlo Ratti has been named the curator of next year's Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism, for which he plans to take "an unconventional, AI-based" approach. Taking place from 24 September 2027, the biennale will be used by Ratti as an opportunity to question the role of a curator today through the lens of architecture. items.summary: AI is increasingly being promoted as a solution to climate change. It can help companies use less fuel, reduce waste and make production more efficient.

items.title: American Airlines flight from San Diego to Chicago diverted to Phoenix Sky Harbor, passenger detained
items.summary: PHOENIX An American Airlines flight traveling from San Diego to Chicago was diverted to Phoenix Sky Harbor Airport overnight after air traffic controllers reported a "Level 3 threat" aboard the plane. items.title: I’m Thankful For My Electric Car
items.summary: I’m a work-from-home writer who loves to drive. So I find myself inventing errands so I have an excuse to explore. I wander in the direction of my destination, chucking detours onto the route to see as much of my town as I can, in as many different conditions as possible. After five years in the same neighborhood of San Diego, I’m still discovering places I love. And today, I’m really grateful that I’m doing it in an EV. It didn’t come naturally to me. I’ve been a fan of gas cars since I was in diapers, clutching a toy car at every hour of the day.

items.title: Linus Torvalds is Angry Again, This Time With ext4 Dev
items.summary: Theodore Ts'o, who maintains ext4, sent Linus Torvalds a pull request of 94 commits for Linux 7.4-rc5, and the merge commit that followed adds 41,204 lines across 68 files. Ts'o said KUnit tests make up most of the added code and exist to help validate patches that AI generates, and that most of the bug fixes in the pull were AI generated as well. What was in the pull that got Torvalds all worked up? Before we dive into that, know that the ext4 filesystem grew out of ext3 and was built to be reliable and to scale to large storage, including filesystems larger than 16TB.

items.summary: The official website for the television anime of Kasumi Yasuda 's Fool Night manga revealed three more cast members on Thursday. items.title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users “DJ their art”
items.summary: In 2017, Apple removed the home button from its iPhones. Users lost a convenient, tangible control — part of a larger shift to digital buttons, knobs, and sliders we also see in cars (like with radio presets and air conditioning) and kitchens (see smart fridges). We can’t leave physical controls behind entirely, though. They tend to be more convenient and efficient — think of how you can use a physical gaming controller without looking at it — and, at times, more precise, like when you use a dial to get the volume just right.

items.title: Budget exhausted: Spain cuts purchase subsidies for electric cars
items.summary: In Spain, the budget for the Auto+ subsidy program for private individuals has been exhausted. The government has allocated €350 million in purchase incentives for electric cars and plug-in hybrids in a short period. What's more, with parliamentary elections approaching in Spain, the funding pot will not be replenished for the foreseeable future.

items.title: St. Mary’s Food Bank gives Thanksgiving meals to 18,882 Arizona families
items.summary: St. Mary’s Food Bank wrapped up its annual holiday food distribution Wednesday after giving complete Thanksgiving meals to 18,882 Arizona families over the past two weeks. St. Mary’s Thanksgiving distribution by the numbers The food bank handed out turkeys and holiday meals to 2,534 families Wednesday, the last of three distribution days in Phoenix and Surprise, said Jerry Brown, its director of public relations. In all, 10,432 families in the two cities received meals over the three days. Assuming five people at each table, Brown said that means more than 94,000 Arizonans will have Thanksgiving dinner Thursday because of the food bank’s distributions and its volunteers and donors.

items.title: Electric trucks in Europe: Why manufacturers are slowing down, and the ICCT remains optimistic
items.summary: The market ramp-up of electric trucks has been delayed by five years, according to European manufacturers. The two perspectives primarily highlight how heavily the development of the electric truck market depends on regulation, economic viability, and infrastructure.

items.title: Docker containers are supposed to be lightweight, so why is my server running out of RAM?
items.summary: Docker containers are lightweight because they share the host operating system’s kernel, eliminating much of the overhead associated with running virtual machines. However, the applications inside those containers still have essentially the same memory requirements as they would if you installed them directly on your server.

items.title: The King’s Unwilling Participants: Civilians and War in Medieval England
items.summary: Civilians supplied the money, food, ships and labour that kept medieval England’s armies fighting. Ilana Krug explores how forced service, corruption and delayed payments made ordinary people reluctant participants in the king’s wars. Civilians have participated – willingly or unwillingly – in war for millennia. Often this is manifest in their victimisation by armies, leading to destroyed villages, plundered goods, and injured or murdered people. Yet, civilians often participate in the war preparation as well, and their involvement in military logistics is clearly visible in the Middle Ages.

items.title: What is a thought made of? Why human consciousness may be beyond AI’s reach
items.summary: A new theory suggests that the brain may chemically encode and retrieve memories rather than relying solely on electrical signals. Researchers propose that interactions between brain cells and their molecular surroundings could help explain the intimate connection between memory, emotion, and thought. items.title: Supercharging transformer residual connections
items.summary: We present DeepCrossAttention (DCA), an architecture that enhances transformer networks by using learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to dynamically combine outputs from previous layers, preventing the information dilution seen in traditional residual connections. Presented in our ICML 2025 paper, this architectural improvement allows models to achieve the same quality up to three times faster with a negligible increase in parameters. Think of a traditional deep learning model like a giant game of "Telephone": data passes through layer after layer, with each layer changing the information slightly.

items.title: American Airlines Flight Chaos as Passenger Attempts to Open Plane Door at Cruising Altitude

The aircraft, operating as Flight 1494 from San Diego International Airport (SAN) to Chicago O’Hare International Airport (ORD), landed in Phoenix at around 1 a.m. local time on November 25, 2026.

items.title: Industry Groups Support Proposed Changes To Pilot Oxygen Rules
items.summary: Aviation groups are backing a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) proposal that would relax requirements for pilots to continuously wear supplemental oxygen masks at higher altitudes. In comments submitted to the FAA, the National Business Aviation Association (NBAA), the National Air Transportation Association (NATA), the Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA) and Vertical Aviation International (VAI) backed proposed changes to oxygen requirements for pressurized aircraft operating under Parts 91 and 135.

items.title: Toyota is about to unveil its first extended-range EV, and it looks like the Highlander
items.summary: Toyota is set to reveal its first extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) on November 27, and from the first look, it could be based on its flagship Highlander SUV. The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs). Unlike fully electric vehicles, an EREV also uses a gas engine that serves as a generator to recharge the battery when it gets low, thereby extending the driving range.

items.title: Crunchyroll’s Hottest Fall 2026 Anime Exposes the Real Problem Behind One-Punch Man
items.summary: J.C. Staff isn’t the problem behind One-Punch Man ‘s disaster, as the studio’s latest anime, currently airing weekly on Crunchyroll, is doing wonders with its animation. Fans often blame J.C. Staff for the decline in quality that plagued the second and third seasons of One-Punch Man. While the second season surprised fans with how much worse it looked compared to the first, the third season, despite taking six years to arrive, somehow looked even worse. It was natural for fans to point their fingers at the studio in charge.

items.title: Recap of Microsoft Ignite 2026: Copilot as the Work OS and Agent Governance
items.summary: At Ignite 2026, Microsoft positioned Copilot as the operating system for work and extended agent identity, governance, and cost controls across Azure, Foundry, Entra, and Defender. Highlights include Cobalt 200 VMs, Azure HorizonDB, a continuous improvement loop in Foundry, Microsoft IQ, a standalone Azure AI Gateway, and Windows Server 2028. By Steef-Jan Wiggers…

items.title: Uber drivers are flocking to EVs amid high gas prices
items.summary: U.S. electric vehicle sales fell off a cliff last year after Republicans deleted the federal EV tax credit. But sky-high gasoline prices are causing EV adoption to soar among one of the populations most exposed to fuel costs: Uber drivers. The ride-hailing company tracks EV adoption on its platform to measure…

items.title: December 2026 Opportunities: Open Calls, Residencies, and Grants for Artists
items.summary: Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly Opportunities Newsletter. Fall $1,800 Innovate Grants for Art + Photo Featured Innovate Grant awards two $1,800 grants each quarter to one visual artist and one photographer. Nine honorable mentions in each category are also featured on the Innovate Grant platform and join a growing creative community of esteemed artists. Applicants must be 18 years and older, and all media and genres are accepted.

items.title: Draining peatlands is responsible for a few percent of our global warming
items.summary: Much of the focus for human-caused climate change is on fossil fuels, which are creating most of our problems. But land use change is also a large component of the story, accounting for about one-third of total historical CO 2 emissions. Deforestation plays a major role here, but practices like draining wetlands also factor in. Exactly how much of our history of eliminating wetlands has contributed to warming is challenging to figure out. But thanks to new sources of data that measure emissions from today’s surviving wetlands, it’s possible to put a better number on it.

items.title: Thom Matthews & Clifton Powell to Star in Demonic Horror Pic ‘Night Tide’
items.summary: Thom Matthews (pictured above in Friday the 13th Part VI: Jason Lives and star of The Return of the Living Dead ) has battled zombies, Jason, and soon he’ll face Hell itself in the indie horror pic Night Tide. Matthews stars alongside Clifton Powell ( Menace II Society, Deep Rising, Bones ), bringing together two cult favorite icons. Here’s the official synopsis: Set in Portland, Maine, in 1996, Night Tide follows Mark Willard and a group of friends who go to a birthday celebration at a drive-in theater.

items.title: nendo on bringing the river-inspired design of france’s TGV INOUI into motion
items.summary: river’s flow becomes visual language for nendo’s train design ‘Unlike cars or airplanes, trains follow tracks along the contours of the landscape, flowing like a river.’ This observation from Japanese design studio nendo became the starting point for the design of France’s TGV INOUI, developed in collaboration with French agency AREP. Now in service, the fifth-generation double-decker train, formerly known as TGV M, brings this idea of flow into the experience of high-speed rail travel. Speaking with designboom, nendo reflects on how this initial reference informed a project that took approximately seven years to develop.

items.title: hoor al qasimi appointed curator of the venice art biennale 2028
items.summary: Hoor Al Qasimi to lead the 2028 Venice Art Biennale Hoor Al Qasimi has been appointed curator of the 62nd Venice Art Biennale, taking on the role of Director of the Visual Arts Department at La Biennale di Venezia ahead of the 2028 edition. The appointment places the Emirati curator in charge of the international exhibition, which opens to the public on April 8 and runs through November 26, 2028. Al Qasimi brings to Venice nearly two decades of experience directing the Sharjah Art Foundation, an institution she established in 2009 to support contemporary art and cultural exchange in the United Arab Emirates and internationally.

items.title: 2026 Was the Year Restaurants Went Full Midwest
items.summary: This is an excerpt from Pre Shift, our newsletter for bartenders, restaurant workers and the hospitality industry. Subscribe for more perspectives like this in your inbox. At Kyle Knall’s Milwaukee restaurant Cassis, the showstopper dish is ravioli Dauphiné, a sheet of 24 tiny squares stuffed with the Wisconsin cheese Pleasant Ridge Reserve. Topped with glazed seasonal veggies, kernels of sweet corn in summer and sliced honeynut squash in late fall, it speaks to Knall’s Midwestern-meets-French approach—one of the reasons why his restaurant earned a slot on Eater’s 2026 list of the Best New Restaurants in America.

items.title: The Suzuki Ignis is back, and this time it will be a low-cost EV sold globally
items.summary: Suzuki offered a first look at the all-new Ignis, its first compact EV designed specifically for global markets. The first-generation Ignis went on sale back in 2000 as a three- and five-door hatchback, and in 2016, Suzuki reintroduced it as a compact crossover. After discontinuing the gas-powered version just last year, Suzuki is now bringing the Ignis back. This time, as a fully electric compact EV. Suzuki revealed the all-new Ignis EV on Wednesday, deeming it the brand’s “first compact EV for global markets.”

items.title: ‘There is no second river we can turn to’: Havasupai Tribe asks for investigation into high levels of arsenic in groundwater
items.summary: PHOENIX – A new analysis by the Grand Canyon Trust of 32 years of groundwater sampling across the Grand Canyon region showed that arsenic levels in monitoring wells near the Pinyon Plain uranium mine were uncharacteristically high. Four wells in the Coconino Aquifer tested positive for arsenic levels above safe drinking water levels in the Grand Canyon region, according to the trust. Three of the wells were at Pinyon Plain Mine, about 40 miles southeast of the Havasupai Indian Reservation, and one was at the Kaibab Plateau north of the Grand Canyon.

items.title: Global stocks rally as investors shrug off U.S. tariffs and AI jitters to 'fish for bargains'
items.summary: Global stocks rallied on Thursday, staging a tentative recovery from an intense AI-driven sell-off and looked past a fresh set of tariffs unveiled by the White House on Wednesday. U.S. markets will be closed Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday and will have a shortened trading session on Friday. During Wednesday's regular session, the Dow gained 0.33%, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62% and the S&P 500 shed 0.25%, with the major averages paring losses seen earlier in the trading day. In Europe on Thursday, equities rose sharply.

items.title: A Sculptural Playground in Shanghai Is Designed for Human-Powered Play
items.summary: In Shanghai’s Jing’an Sculpture Park, a monumental new installation by Brooklyn’s Wade and Leta has a clear goal: to get people up and moving in the same space. Titled “Catching Feelings,” the interactive artwork doubles as an all-ages playground with the artists’ signature sculptures and geometric forms. A central tower holds a quartet of slides, while other spinning and writhing elements are designed for more unstructured interaction. “Catching Feelings” is one of 36 projects in the ninth edition of the Jing’an International Sculpture Project, an annual project helmed by the UCCA Center for Contemporary Art.

items.title: Meet Warty, the AI Launcher Canonical Is Building for Ubuntu
items.summary: Back in April, Canonical shared its plans for AI in Ubuntu, favoring models that run on the user's own hardware and open-weight options over cloud services. The plan also split AI features as behind-the-scenes improvements to existing parts of the OS and visible, as well as agentic ones that users opt into. Myna came next, a speech-to-text tool that runs on local models. It debuted as an optional preview in Ubuntu 26.10, and the company says it will ship by default with Ubuntu 28.04 LTS. More recently, Canonical introduced Surge at Ubuntu Summit 26.10.

items.title: Where scientists draw the line on AI agents
items.summary: Delegating research tasks to AI does not remove scientists’ responsibility for how the work is accomplished. For example, a researcher using AI to review the literature needs to check whether the system overlooks conflicting evidence or makes claims the cited papers don’t support. Someone handing off data analysis to an agentic system needs to understand which methods it used, which files it accessed, and whether the results can be successfully reproduced.

items.title: American Airlines Pilot Received A Cockpit Alert — An Air Traffic Control Says They’ve “Had Alien Sightings Out There”
items.summary: A pilot flying from Washington National airport to Philadelphia for American Airlines subsidiary PSA got a cockpit traffic alert near Baltimore. The air traffic controller told him he’d already passed the only airplane she could see nearby. Then she added, “I mean, we have had alien sightings out there, so…”

items.title: Two screenings of Pakistani TV show cancelled in India after backlash
items.summary: Until Wednesday, the weekend plans of some television enthusiasts in the Indian city of Bengaluru involved dressing up, having an elaborate dinner and finding out what happens next in the lives of a wildly popular fictional Pakistani couple. Two private screenings of Dar-e-Nijaat (Door to Salvation), a Pakistani television drama that has become something of a sensation on Indian social media, were called off after an online backlash and police scrutiny. The serial, which airs on Pakistan's ARY Digital, is available to Indian viewers through some YouTube channels, though the broadcaster's official channel is blocked in India.

items.title: Chile Is Getting a Massive New National Park in 2027
items.summary: If you’ve already hiked the W Trek in Torres del Paine, you may want to start looking a little farther south for your next trip to Patagonia. Chile is planning to establish a new national park in 2027, at the southernmost point of mainland South America, about 40 miles south of Punta Arenas. In early November 2026, conservation nonprofit Rewilding Chile signed an agreement with the Chilean government to donate an additional 55,186 acres of land toward the creation of Cape Froward National Park (Parque Nacional Cabo Froward).

items.title: clustered cycladic village residences shape aristides dallas architects’ hospitality masterplan
items.summary: ARISTIDES DALLAS STAGGERS HILLSIDE VOLUMES for resort in CYCLADES Sited on a sloping hillside on a Greek island in the Cyclades, angled away from the sea, Shared Ground is a hospitality masterplan by Aristides Dallas Architects organized around topography and sightlines. To capture Aegean views without imposing a rigid grid on the slope, the studio arranges staggered low-rise volumes along the natural contours, orienting each building obliquely toward the water while preserving privacy across the site.

items.title: Ancient Cahokia transformed amid droughts and flooding—climate change is reshaping modern communities in similar ways
items.summary: More than 800 years ago, a combination of environmental and societal challenges led some Mississippian people to leave Cahokia, a massive archaeological site that was once home to 20,000 people near modern-day St. Louis. Just south of Cahokia, another archaeological site is taking shape at Centreville, Illinois, as modern-day people abandon their homes in the face of 21st-century climate and cultural changes.

items.title: Switzerland’s biggest bank set for showdown with lawmakers as capital fight intensifies amid crisis planning
items.summary: UBS 's crisis planning has won qualified support from market regulators, which called its plan "executable" in principle. But Switzerland's biggest bank still faces a major fight over sweeping plans that would force it to hold more capital against its foreign subsidiaries. FINMA, the Swiss markets regulator, said Wednesday that UBS's resolvability — or its ability to fail safely, without wreaking havoc on the economy — has improved since it integrated rival Credit Suisse, with progress made in implementing the emergency plan across group-wide resolution planning.

items.title: GTA 6 could've had tennis, Sims 4-style house decorating, crafting, and more – but Rockstar cut it
items.summary: GTA 6 might just be one of the biggest games of all time, with a map so vast it rivals the combined maps of GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 – but, believe it or not, Rockstar cut some features from the new Grand Theft Auto. Yes, that's right – it could've been even bigger. It's difficult to fathom, but Rockstar leads Rob Nelson and Scott Mitchell reveal some of what was cut in a new interview with PCGames. The outlet first asks them about a tennis minigame, which exists in GTA 5. The two admit that developers initially planned to include tennis, but they weren't happy with how it was turning out, so they eventually axed it from the game.

items.title: Staff at Anthropic and Open AI sound alarm on advanced models too powerful to release
items.summary: Employees working at frontier artificial intelligence model companies Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC have been butting heads with executives over advanced models whose reasoning is such that the models pose to danger to humanity, according to a report by Axios today based on more than two dozen sources familiar with the current standoff at…

items.title: Form and diversity: How tumor architecture shapes colorectal cancer progression
items.summary: Tumors are not uniform, as even cancer cells within one patient can display extremely divergent characteristics and behaviors. This diversity, known as tumor heterogeneity, reduces therapeutic efficacy because cells in different states may respond differently to therapeutic interventions.

items.title: Stronger molecular grip optimizes anticancer drug release
items.summary: Researchers from Osaka Metropolitan University have modified a naturally occurring protein so that it can hold on to an anticancer drug more tightly, potentially preventing the drug from being released before it reaches its intended destination.

items.title: Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease
items.summary: A combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin produced results comparable to antibiotics when used alongside standard treatment for severe gum disease, with benefits persisting long after supplementation ended. The surprising discovery could offer an alternative for some patients while reducing reliance on antibiotics.

items.title: Tunnels Underneath Hagia Sophia Excavated
items.summary: ISTANBUL, TURKEY— Hürriyet Daily News reports that some 3,000 tons of debris has been removed from the tunnels beneath the Vezir Garden and West Garden sections of Hagia Sophia, a structure completed in A.D. 537 during the rule of the Byzantine emperor Justinian I (reigned A.D. 527–565). The more than 1,300 feet of tunnels are thought to have been part of the city’s drainage system, explained Mehmet Nuri Ersoy, Turkey’s Culture and Tourism Minister. As the debris was cleared, researchers repaired damaged vaults and reinforced sections of the tunnels with stainless steel supports.

items.title: Risk for disease flare low for women with IBD undergoing assisted reproductive technology
items.summary: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART) have low flare rates and live birth rates comparable to those of the general population, according to a study published online Nov. 10 in Inflammatory Bowel Diseases.

items.title: This 345-million-year-old fossil had scientists fooled for decades
items.summary: A famous 345-million-year-old fossil has turned out to be something entirely different from what scientists believed for decades. Advanced X-ray imaging revealed hidden gills and thousands of tiny teeth, exposing a primitive aquatic or amphibious creature rather than an early reptile. The discovery suggests that several adaptations associated with life on land actually evolved in animals still dependent on water.

items.title: New FAA Rule For Planes Lining Up On Runways May Cause Delays
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has just added some new restrictions to how air traffic controllers can clear aircraft to “line up and wait” on the runway, in anticipation of takeoff clearance. This is intended to add an extra safety buffer, but to quote an airline pilot on an ATC frequency, “that’s probably going to cause some delays, that’s for sure.” New restrictions on planes holding on runway for takeoff As of today (November 24, 2026), the FAA has introduced a new rule regarding how aircraft can be cleared onto runways at airports.

items.title: Union Veterans and the Bitter Aftermath of the Civil War
items.summary: In the decade following the Civil War, many white northerners wanted nothing more than to put the carnage behind them and reunify the country. But, historian Brian Matthew Jordan writes, one group that generally wasn’t ready to forgive and forget was Union veterans. Jordan writes that the returning soldiers found a society that was happy to hail them as heroes but often offered them little material support. Many employers refused to hire men who they believed were too mentally or physically wounded to function.

items.title: Medicare Open Enrollment: Here’s What’s Changing, and What Mistakes To Avoid
items.summary: Annual open enrollment is underway for Medicare, the federal program that provides health insurance to roughly 70 million people. The coverage choices are complex and often consequential. Medicare provides health insurance to people 65 or older, as well as to some younger people with disabilities or certain health conditions. But it isn’t one plan. It’s more like a build-your-own-insurance menu. Roughly half of beneficiaries are enrolled in traditional Medicare, which consists of Parts A and B. Administered by the federal government, the plan covers hospital stays, skilled nursing care, doctor visits, outpatient care, and preventive screenings.

items.title: Acheulean Hand Axes Found in Kalahari Desert
items.summary: GABORONE, BOTSWANA—Close to 100 Acheulean hand axes have been found in the Okwa Valley of the Kalahari Desert, according to a Science in Poland report. Acheulean tools were first crafted some 1.7 million years ago, during the Pleistocene, when there was a network of rivers and lakes in the area. Many of these hand axes were recovered near the shoreline of an ancient body of water. “The Okwa Valley is an exceptionally challenging area for research,” said Mirosław Masojć of the University of Wrocław.

items.title: Ptolemaic Foundation Unearthed in Alexandria
items.summary: ALEXANDRIA, EGYPT— Ahram Online reports that a foundation made of limestone blocks, a tunnel, and a surrounding wall have been uncovered at the Shallalat Gardens site in the Royal Quarter of ancient Alexandria by researchers from the Hellenic Research Institute of Alexandrian Civilization (HRIAC). A committee of experts headed by Ayman Ashmawy of Egypt’s Supreme Council of Antiquities examined the square-shaped foundation and determined that it likely supported a tall building, which may have had a funerary function, based on the architectural features recovered at the site.

items.title: Poundland collapses putting 11,000 jobs at risk
items.summary: Poundland has collapsed into administration, putting 11,000 jobs at risk, after its owners failed to find a buyer to keep it in business. The retailer's shops and distribution centres will remain open and continue to trade during the administration process with the business likely to be broken up and some of its stores sold off to rival retailers. Poundland's US owners held talks with several bidders over a last-minute rescue deal, but no agreement was reached. Poundland boss Barry Williams said in a note to staff that the board had "no alternative but to take this decision", but was making it with "sincere sadness and intense regret".

items.title: The Best Single-Serve Coffee Maker for All the Pod People Out There (2026)
items.summary: Try as we might, there’s just no changing the hearts and minds of some people, even our dearest loved ones, by presenting them with inconvenient truths. I’m talking, of course, about people who prefer coffee from pods. But based on the popularity of coffee pod machines, it seems those of us who haven’t been assimilated into pod people are outnumbered. And, to be fair, even if the quality of their coffee is all over the place, we can’t deny their convenience. My goal here is to find single-serve coffee makers that can blend that convenience with coffee I actually want to drink.

items.title: Early Stone Age rock carvings in Scandinavia may have been signposts for hunting grounds
items.summary: Between roughly 9,000 and 4,000 B.C., artists in ancient Scandinavia painstakingly carved large, sometimes life-size images of elk, reindeer, bears and other creatures into rock faces teetering on the edge of fjords, rivers and lakes. But their meaning has long been debated.

items.title: Winter Bivy Sack Guide (2026)
items.summary: Winter bivy sacks were first developed as solo shelters for mountaineering and climbing where participants were interested in lightweight and highly compressible camping gear. Bivy Sacks are also an attractive option for backpacking hunters, backcountry skiers, and winter backpackers who want the lightest and smallest shelter they can carry for overnight or emergency use. items.title: Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS vs. Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS Benchmarks
items.summary: System76 released Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS yesterday as the newest version of their Ubuntu-derived Linux distribution featuring their in-house COSMIC desktop environment. For those curious about any performance differences out of Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS, I already have some benchmarks comparing it to the former 24.04 release since the new System76 Thelio Prime SFF PC has been shipping with 26.04 LTS since last week.

items.title: ‘Day Drinker’: Johnny Depp’s Supernatural Revenge Thriller Rated R for Strong Bloody Violence
items.summary: Johnny Depp’s next supernatural thriller is bringing the blood. Day Drinker has officially been rated R for “strong bloody violence, language and brief drug use,” Dread Central learned today. Directed by Marc Webb ( The Amazing Spider-Man ), the Lionsgate film mixes a criminal conspiracy with a teased ghost story. As we covered when the first trailer arrived, there appears to be considerably more going on here than a mysterious guy ordering another drink. Madelyn Cline ( I Know What You Did Last Summer ) plays a bartender aboard a private yacht who encounters an unusual guest, played by Depp ( Sleepy Hollow, Ebenezer ).

items.title: How ‘Fool Night’ Gave ‘Jujutsu Kaisen’ Star Adam McArthur His Saddest Anime Boy Yet
items.summary: Fool Night is set in a future where the sun hasn’t shone in more than a century. As Earth’s plant life withers and oxygen levels continue to fall, scientists develop transfloration, a controversial process that turns people into plants to keep society alive. Or so they say. It’s a tough pitch for recruiters like deuteragonist Yomiko Horai, even with the financial incentives offered to volunteers like our hero (and Yomiko’s childhood best friend) Toshiro Kamiya. Toshiro is as desperate as an anime protagonist has ever been.

items.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
items.summary: The US has announced a fresh raft of tariffs as President Donald Trump pushes ahead with his signature trade policy. The new taxes charged on imports to America are set to hit many of the country's biggest trading partners - China, the European Union and 12 other jurisdictions, including Japan, South Korea and Taiwan. The White House began investigating the trade practices of other countries in March after the US Supreme Court ruled Trump's previously announced Liberation Day tariffs were illegal.

items.title: Wealthy Europeans look beyond stocks amid AI selloff. Here’s where they’re investing
items.summary: Wealthy Europeans are looking to alternative asset classes to build exposure to artificial intelligence themes amid turbulence in public markets. Goldman Sachs Alternatives' inaugural survey of high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth investors found 47% of European respondents saw alternatives as the best way to gain exposure to AI and future tech growth, compared to just 24% of U.S. investors. The survey found a significant gap between the U.S. and Europe in terms of investor knowledge of alternatives, which include assets like private equity, property and infrastructure.

items.title: 3 Anime to Watch If You’re Waiting for Re:Zero Season 5
items.summary: Re:Zero -Starting Life in Another World – is easily one of the biggest anime on Crunchyroll, and it continues to get more popular thanks to its sequel seasons. 2026 was a huge year for fans since the anime not only commemorated its 10th anniversary, but also aired its Season 4 in two cours. Written by Tappei Nagatsuki, Re:Zero is one of the most intense dark fantasies that doesn’t shy away from showing the brutalities of the world Subaru is forced to live in. The fourth season was one of the biggest anime of the year as it continues Subaru’s gruesome journey where he is forced to witness his friends die in gruesome ways, forcing him to realize his own weakness.

items.title: World's fastest animal could nearly double its livable territory by 2080 in the UK due to climate change
items.summary: Global warming and climate change could have the unexpected bounty of making Great Britain a more welcoming home for the fastest animal on Earth. The area suitable for peregrine falcons within the UK could grow by 74% by the year 2080 under a high-emissions climate scenario, a new study has shown.

items.title: Subnautica 2 dates its Tar Trek content update for December 1
items.summary: Over the past few weeks, Subnautica 2 has been putting out video digests that talk about its next content update, but mostly from a high level view without too many specifics. Obviously that’s changing now, as Unknown Worlds has tied down a Tuesday, December 1st release date for this content. It’s even given it a punny name:…

items.title: Three LLM inflection points in twelve months
items.summary: I gave a keynote at the AI Engineer Code Summit a couple of weeks ago, constructed around the idea that there have been three significant inflection points in the abilities of LLMs and coding agents in the past twelve months. Here's the video of the talk. In this post I'm going to pull out the major inflection point theme and interrogate it more deeply. Coding agents in November 2025 Today, November 24th 2026, is the one year anniversary of the release of Claude Opus 4.5. With hindsight, this was a consequential model.

items.title: Striped Malted Pound Cake
items.summary: My earliest dessert obsession was the malted milkshake, which I indulged in every time I had enough babysitting money. My oldest, best friend, Toi, was equally obsessed with Whoppers, and we both wondered why malted sweets were so good. Turns out, the secret is in the combination of malted barley, wheat flour, and evaporated whole milk that gets toasted to caramelize the sugars contained in it. This cake is my latest malted creation. Layering the malted vanilla and chocolate batters so they create a striped pattern isn’t just an aesthetic choice.

items.title: What is holding back bidirectional EV charging as a grid resource?
items.summary: Costs remain high and tech solutions are incomplete, but experts say careful utility program design and a new generation of vehicle charging solutions will bring value to both consumers and the grid.

items.title: Run with the Semi-Wild Yilki Horses of Anatolia in Nur Tucker’s Captivating Photos
items.summary: Around the dusty plains and otherworldly volcanic rock formations of the historical region of Cappadocia, a millennia-old tradition continues. Here in Central Anatolia, Turkey, horses have been a part of daily life, civic programs, and military campaigns since prehistory. In The Untold Story of the Yilki Horse, photographer Nur Tucker captures a portrait of the region’s living heritage. Published by Hemeria, the title delves into the beauty and tenacity of the semi-wild horses while also highlighting the lifestyles of those who herd them through rugged landscapes.

items.title: Scientists discover mysterious lakes more than a mile beneath the Red Sea
items.summary: More than a mile beneath the surface of the Red Sea, scientists have discovered rare underwater lakes that could reveal secrets about Earth's ancient oceans and the possibility of alien life. Known as brine pools, these extremely salty, oxygen-free environments are surprisingly teeming with microbial life, challenging our understanding of where living organisms can survive.

items.title: ‘Ugly and mishmashy’ U.S. solar manufacturing policy leaves important questions unanswered
items.summary: In the years since the passage of the Inflation Reduction Act in 2022, the United States solar manufacturing sector has seen growth in its capacity to produce finished modules using domestic components that might have seemed unimaginable prior to the law’s introduction. Spurred by the manufacturing production tax credits under Section 45X, domestic solar module nameplate capacity has increased from less than 10 GW four years ago to a reported 80.6 GW today, according to the latest numbers from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA ).

items.title: Astronomers may have discovered a black hole born before the first stars
items.summary: A mysterious object named Phoebe, detected when it briefly magnified a distant star, could be a primordial black hole formed just after the Big Bang. With an estimated mass only three times that of the Moon, it may be a 13-billion-year-old cosmic relic that offers new clues to the mystery of dark matter.

items.title: After 15 years on Ubuntu Server, Debian 13 might finally win me over
items.summary: If you’re like me, then you probably reach for Ubuntu as a default server distro out of habit. I’ve done that for nearly 15 years. The problem is, Ubuntu isn’t what it used to be, and Debian is. Starting with Ubuntu 25.10, Canonical began the migration from using GNU’s core utilities to all-new Rust-based coreutils.

items.title: Still Sidelined: Former coaches, players lament loss of opportunities with dissolution of Arizona JUCO football
items.summary: PHOENIX – Donnie Yantis promised his mother before she died that he would return to college and earn his degree, but after struggling academically and stepping away from football, he needed a second chance to fulfill his pledge. That opportunity came from then-Glendale Community College football coach Joe Kersting, who welcomed Yantis back to the program and helped him find direction both on and off the field. Yantis graduated in December 1992, then continued his education and became a high school and college coach.

items.title: Miami runway incident disrupts flights on Thanksgiving eve
items.summary: Thanksgiving travellers in the US have run into disruption after an incident at one of the nation's busiest airports caused hours-long delays. On Wednesday, the eve of the holiday, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) briefly grounded all flights heading for Miami International Airport, after a FedEx aircraft overran one of the runways. No injuries were reported, and the FAA is investigating what happened. It had previously warned that delays across the country would be possible "throughout the week" as a result of severe weather, including heavy rain and wind that are forecast in eastern areas on Thursday.

items.title: Novel Experiments Expand the Hunt for ‘Ultralight’ Dark Matter
items.summary: Click to tell Google to prioritize Quanta and see more of the best coverage of science and math in your search and AI results. Almost a century ago — in 1933, to be exact — Fritz Zwicky’s studies of distant galaxies led him to suggest that “dark matter is present in very much greater density than luminous matter.” Observations by the astronomer Vera Rubin would later substantiate the case for the intangible, leading her to write in 1980 that “the conclusion is inescapable that non-luminous matter exists.”

items.title: World’s largest trial of robotic knee replacement reveals surprising results
items.summary: Robot-assisted knee replacement surgery offers greater surgical precision, but a landmark clinical trial has revealed a surprising limitation. Despite the advanced technology, patients experienced no meaningful improvements in pain, mobility, or recovery compared with conventional surgery after one year.

items.title: Qantas Boeing 737 Aborts Landing at Sydney Airport After Air New Zealand A321 Crosses Runway
items.summary: SYDNEY – A Qantas (QF) flight from Melbourne to Sydney performed an unexpected go-around after its pilots identified an Air New Zealand aircraft crossing the runway moments before landing at Sydney Airport (SYD). The incident occurred on Wednesday morning, November 25, 2026, when the approaching aircraft was approximately 90 metres above the ground. The Qantas crew initiated the manoeuvre to avoid a potential runway collision, as the Air New Zealand (NZ) aircraft had not cleared the runway. The flight subsequently completed another approach and landed safely, while the incident has prompted a new investigation by Australia’s aviation safety regulator.

items.title: 1Password Confirms Security Breach, Customer Account Data Stolen
items.summary: 1Password has announced a security breach that has resulted in customer account information and its proprietary source code being stolen. They have, however, stated that the encrypted password vaults and the passwords themselves were not compromised. In a security incident disclosure, the company said it had begun an investigation into the compromise of an employee’s corporate GitHub account six days earlier. The attacker used the compromised account to access internal repos and inject malicious code into backend services, enabling them to pull customer account records.

items.title: Mellum2.1 Instruct Is Out, Bringing Faster Answers for Coding Agents
items.summary: The faster sibling of Mellum2.1 Thinking, built for sub-agents, tool loops, and chat. In October, we released Mellum2.1 Thinking, an open 12B mixture-of-experts model with 2.5B active parameters, trained to work as a coding agent. Today, we are releasing its sibling, Mellum2.1 Instruct. It is built on the same architecture and trained identically, but it gives straight answers without including its chain of thought.

items.title: Tributes for Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor after his death aged 65
items.summary: Simon Le Bon, Sir Rod Stewart and Gary Kemp are among the pop stars who have paid tribute to Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor following his death at the age of 65. Taylor co-wrote some of the group's biggest hits including Save A Prayer, Rio and Girls On Film. Le Bon and his bandmates paid tribute, saying "he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music", while Sir Rod remembered his "dear pal" and Spandau Ballet's Kemp called him "a great player who set the tone for the 80s". Taylor's wife Tracey called him "the rock of our family", adding: "We will miss him every single day."

items.title: California warns of flooding as King Tides peak over Thanksgiving
items.summary: Coastal areas of California are bracing for potential flooding as king tides peak in the state during the US Thanksgiving holiday. Water levels across the US state's vast coastline could reach over 8ft (2.4 metres) in some areas on Wednesday and Thursday, according to the National Weather Service (NWS) - breaking records set just last month. The NWS has warned parts of California could face major coastal flooding, which is likely to be significant in low-lying areas. There have already been some reports of flooding.

items.title: Mitsubishi Electric Research Lab CEO on How He Reached the C-Suite
items.summary: The trajectory from researcher to top executive at a leading R&D organization doesn’t happen overnight. It took Anthony Vetro nearly 30 years to climb the corporate ladder at Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories, in Cambridge, Mass. He joined MERL in 1996, right out of college, and he has worked there ever since. Vetro probably is best known for his research in multimedia signal processing, focusing on video compression. Anthony Vetro Employer Mitsubishi Electric Research Laboratories, in Cambridge, Mass.

items.title: Compact Edge AI camera packs Raspberry Pi CM5, Hailo-8 NPU, 12MP sensor, speaker and microphone
items.summary: Hellbender Tendryl Camera is an edge AI camera that integrates a Raspberry Pi CM5 module, a Hailo-8 AI accelerator, and a 12MP Raspberry Pi Camera Module 3, as well as a speaker and microphone, into a compact fanless enclosure. The camera features a CM5 module with 4GB of RAM, a 16GB eMMC flash, and a wireless module for WiFi 5 and Bluetooth 5.0 connectivity. Other features include a Gigabit Ethernet with PoE+, a full-sized HDMI output port, three USB-C ports for power, data, and OS flashing, a 6-axis IMU, and a temperature, humidity, and pressure sensor.

items.title: Brad Pitt's $224 Million Horror Classic Officially Leaves Streaming
items.summary: Given that Tom Cruise and Brad Pitt have been two of Hollywood's biggest stars for the best part of three decades, it's quite remarkable that we've only ever seen the pair in one movie together, although Pitt did come close to working with Cruise again when the two were attached to an earlier version of Ford v Ferrari. Their only collaboration to date came in 1994, the same year Pitt worked with Anthony Hopkins on Legends of the Fall, and just two years before Cruise established what would become his most successful franchise with Mission: Impossible.

items.summary: No serious injuries were reported in the crash near Baseline and McQueen roads.

items.title: Dinosaurs likely tore meat like birds of prey
items.summary: Meat-eating dinosaurs probably fed by dragging their teeth backward through flesh like a saw rather than biting straight down like a dagger, new experiments suggest.

items.title: Giant deer bones may push human arrival in Ireland back by 1,000 years
items.summary: A team of archaeologists and scientists has uncovered tantalizing new evidence that Late Upper Paleolithic hunter-gatherers may have lived in southern Ireland around 13,500 years ago—nearly a millennium earlier than currently confirmed.

items.title: PipeWire 1.6.12 Multimedia Framework Improves Video Capture and JACK Stability
items.summary: PipeWire 1.6.12 has been released as a maintenance update to the Linux multimedia framework, improving video capture compatibility, fixing JACK audio threading issues, and resolving several crashes and deadlocks. On the video side, the release improves V4L2 compatibility with problematic drivers, adds validation checks, corrects property enumeration, and improves error handling. It also introduces compatibility with libcamera 0.8. JACK users gain from a fix for a potential deadlock during shutdown and corrected event queue thread handling.

items.title: James ‘Fergie’ Chambers: US trying to cast ‘antiwar ideas as extremist’
items.summary: Madrid, Spain – James “Fergie” Chambers, a pro-Palestine philanthropist who is the subject of an ongoing extradition request by the United States government, said he believed the US is targeting supporters of the people of Gaza worldwide. The US government’s case centres on Chambers’s alleged laundering of $7.5m, which he is said to have wired several years ago from a US bank account to Tunisia, where he lived at the time, allegedly using the cash to support Hamas. He is not charged with any “terrorism” offences and denies any wrongdoing.

items.title: How Trump’s latest tariff moves hand India an edge over rival Asian exporters
items.summary: The latest U.S. tariff rates announced Wednesday have signaled that Washington is willing to offer India an edge over its competitors if New Delhi agrees to finalize a long-pending trade deal. The Office of the United States Trade Representative has proposed a tariff of 17% on Indian exports if New Delhi "were to reach an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade" with Washington. It added that without a trade deal, India could face tariffs of up to 25% under Section 301 investigations encompassing excess production capacity that harms U.S. interests.

items.title: Why the Battle of Red Cliffs Was the Ultimate Turning Point in Chinese History
items.summary: China has long had a history of unity followed by division, and the Battle of Red Cliffs stands out as a key event that contributed significantly to this pattern. It took place towards the end of the Han Dynasty and stopped Cao Cao, a powerful northern warlord who controlled much of northern China, from conquering the lands south of the Yangtze River. Had he won the battle, East Asia would have remained a unified country, as the Three Kingdoms period would not have emerged to divide it. Why Cao Cao Chained His Fleet—And How It Ruined His Southern Campaign The Battle of Red Cliffs began following the campaign by the northern warlord Cao Cao to conquer the south.

items.title: A cosmically close supernova may spill the stellar explosion’s secrets
items.summary: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey. (See our AI policy here.) When astronomers first spotted the supernova now designated SN 2026ahvu, it was just one of the dozens detected every day. But scientists soon realized this one was something very special, and they’ve been hustling to study it ever since. “I think almost everyone in the world is trying to trigger a telescope and look at this,” says astrophysicist Sumit Sarbadhicary of Johns Hopkins University. Soon after scientists spotted the explosion on November 2, they determined it hadn’t yet peaked in brightness, giving scientists an early glimpse at the event.

items.title: Extinct, long-legged grasshoppers walked on water alongside dinosaurs
items.summary: Nearly 100 million years ago, spindly legged grasshoppers may have scooted across water like modern day water striders. The clues are in the fossilized insects’ legs and feet. Special hairs and leaf-shaped leg adornments, exquisitely preserved in amber, suggest the insects — members of a newfound family of insects — could balance and slide around on surface tension, researchers report November 24 in Proceedings of the Royal Society B. The discovery suggests at least three insect groups evolved independently to move across water.

items.title: ‘Blade Runner 2099’ Easter Eggs, Callbacks & References to the Original Films Explained
items.summary: Did you catch all these references? Prime Video's Blade Runner 2099 doesn't just expand the dystopian world first introduced in Ridley Scott's 1982 sci-fi classic. It also pays tribute to the franchise's past, packing its eight episodes with callbacks, Easter eggs, and references to the films, as well as Philip K. Dick's novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, which started it all.

items.title: Iraq denies reports of troop movements towards Kurdish region
items.summary: Iraq’s government has denied local media reports that army units were moving towards the Kurdistan region, as a top court backed Baghdad’s authority over the region’s border crossings and oil in a deepening dispute with Erbil. Government spokesperson Haidar al-Aboudi told state broadcaster Al-Iraqiya on Wednesday that there was “no truth” to the media reports. He said oil smugglers were diverting “tens of billions” into “private pockets and accounts”, and that the salaries of Kurdistan’s public employees were not part of the dispute.

items.title: Suspect indicted for explosion at SRP substation in Mesa
items.summary: The suspect is accused of causing an explosion at a substation that supplies power to a data center.

items.title: HOA neighborhood residents are looking to face higher water bill costs as commercial surcharges are applied.
items.summary: PHOENIX – Residents in homeowners association neighborhoods could see significant increases in their water bills as the city searches for solutions to save. Amanda McGowan lives in the Stetson Valley, located just off of I-17 and W Happy Valley Rd in north Phoenix. She is president of the Stetson Valley Owners Association Board and her community could be facing up to $30,000 in surcharges on its water bills each year based on past water use averages.

items.title: Carbon nanotube measurements reveal quantum model better explains collective electron behavior
items.summary: An international team of scientists from Lithuania, Finland and Israel has conducted both theoretical and experimental research into carbon nanotubes, becoming the first to demonstrate which physical model governs the motion and interactions of electrons within them.

items.title: Australia’s legless geckos evolved like snakes did
items.summary: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback? Take our survey. (See our AI policy here.) Australia’s limbless geckos look a lot like snakes. It turns out they’ve evolved like snakes too. Snakes are technically a highly modified group of legless lizards. Dozens of other lizard lineages have independently lost their legs, too. But the legless pygopod geckos aren’t quite like their slithering nonsnake kin. Pygopods have dietary pickiness and physical diversity patterns that are more reminiscent of those found in snakes than in other legless lizards, researchers report in a preprint posted at bioRxiv.org on October 23.

items.title: Ukrainian combat laser shoots down Russian jet-powered Geran drone
items.summary: A laser air defense system developed by Ukrainian company Carmine Sky has reportedly shot down a Russian jet-powered Geran drone, according to Serhii “Flash” Beskrestnov, a radio technology specialist and adviser to Ukraine’s president. In a Telegram post on November 25, 2026, Beskrestnov said the Blysk laser, deployed to protect a critical infrastructure facility, had become the first combat laser in the world to shoot down a jet-powered Geran. Geran is Russia’s designation for its Shahed-type one-way attack drones.

items.title: Health issues delay trial of Berlin woman accused of spying for Russia
items.summary: The trial of a German-Ukrainian woman on charges of spying for Russia due to start Thursday was delayed in the morning after the accused developed health problems that required treatment by emergency medical workers, a spokeswoman for a Berlin court said. The arrest of the 57-year-old Berlin businesswoman triggered a diplomatic clash between Berlin and Moscow. Ilona W., who holds German and Ukrainian citizenship, is accused of working for the intelligence service of a foreign power. Her full name has not been released due to German privacy laws.

items.title: Emirates and Etihad A380 aircraft among eight requiring EASA ordered inspections
items.summary: Emirates and Etihad Airways Airbus A380 aircraft are among eight superjumbos that must undergo inspections after the European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) issued an Airworthiness Directive raising concerns around a “potential unsafe condition”. The Airworthiness Directive (2026-0216) supersedes a previous instruction (2026-0119-E) issued in June 2026, requiring 16 Airbus A380s to receive wing mid spars inspections. EASA previously said that this “condition, if not detected and corrected, could reduce the structural integrity of the wing”.

items.title: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
items.summary: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer.

items.title: Ukraine drone attack kills five in Russian-occupied Zaporizhia
items.summary: At least five people have been killed and three others were wounded in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russian-occupied Zaporizhia, a Russian-installed official said, as Russian forces hit Ukraine’s capital Kyiv in a ballistic missile assault. “Following an enemy drone attack on a parking lot, five people were killed and three others wounded in the locality of Vesioloye,” Moscow-installed governor Yevgeny Balitsky wrote on Telegram on Thursday. Earlier, Ukrainian forces hit a major Russian military base east of Moscow, damaging five aircraft used to launch missiles and bombs, according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

items.title: Peppermint Mocha Pistachio Milk, Olive Wood Steak Knives, and More Things BA Editors Loved in November
items.summary: As people who write about food and kitchen gadgets for a living, Bon Appétit editors are constantly surrounded by a wide range of products. Between our own purchases and the endless stream of samples sent our way, it means there’s always something new coming across our desks and into our homes. Each month we round up the standouts we tested or bought ourselves that changed the way we cook and eat. This month, holiday-ready martini glasses, turmeric-laced bone broth, and digestion-friendly tea. Read on for all the products we obsessed over in November.

items.title: While Exploring a 500-Year-Old Shipwreck Off the Coast of Sweden, Underwater Archaeologists Discovered Medieval Chain Mail That May Have Belonged to German Mercenaries
items.summary: More than five centuries after a royal Danish warship exploded and sank off the coast of Sweden, underwater archaeologists have uncovered finely crafted chain mail armor resting on the Baltic seafloor. The copper-alloy mail fragments were recovered in October from the wreck of Gribshunden, or Griffin, the 15th-century flagship of King Hans of Denmark and Norway. Researchers discovered the armor alongside a rare munitions chest while surveying the area beneath the vessel’s forecastle, an elevated combat platform at the ship’s bow.

items.title: Sticker Shock Looms as a Major Challenge in Push for Single-Payer Healthcare
items.summary: As an Oregon panel finalized its proposal for statewide universal healthcare this month, opposition had already coalesced around a familiar theme: The costs and the new taxes needed to support it will be staggeringly large. The panel’s estimates place the cost of the plan at $69.7 billion a year starting in 2032. The same arguments are being made on the national level about “Medicare for All,” which gained renewed life after Democrats’ victorious blue wave in the midterms. One recent White House cost estimate pegged the annual price tag at $4.7 trillion.

items.title: The Australian Shuffle
items.summary: Shuffle a deck of cards and divide it into four packets. Pick up any packet, look at the top card, and remember it. Spell out the phrase AUSTRALIAN SHUFFLE, transferring one card from the top to the bottom of the packet for each letter. Now apply the phrase Down Under — put the top card down on the table, and the next card under the packet. Continue doing this until you’re holding a single card. It’s the card you memorized. ( By Josh Jay, based on a principle discovered by Alex Elmsley. )
