items.summary: The injured bicyclist was found lying in a construction area near 15th and Peoria avenues on Nov. 22.

items.title: Norse Atlantic suspends all flights as it faces potential collapse
items.summary: The Norwegian low cost carrier Norse Atlantic Airways has suspended all flights as it rushes to resolve what it warned is a critical financial situation. The airline said if no solution can be found, it intends to file for bankruptcy. The airline uses a fleet of 12 Boeing 787 aircraft on long-haul routes from a number of European airports, including London Gatwick, Rome and Oslo. Prior to the suspension of flights, it was advertising services from London to Orlando, Cape Town, Bangkok and Phuket.

items.title: EU leaders seek agreement on long-term budget and Ukraine at summit
items.summary: Russia has criticized the European Union's proposed seven-year budget, accusing the bloc of seeking to prolong the war in Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the EU's plans to allocate money for Ukraine in its budget would make Kyiv "less inclined toward a peace process and more determined to continue the war." Peskov said the result would be more military spending, leaving less for governments to spend on school, hospitals and social facilities. Support for Ukraine is among the key areas of discussion in the 2028-2034 budget which includes up to €100 billion for Ukraine, however diplomats say this figure falls well short of Kyiv's needs.

items.title: Cost of living roadshow highlights support on offer
items.summary: A cost of living roadshow held in a Kent town is the "starting point" and "first step on the ladder" to resolve financial problems, a local councillor has said. Organisations, including those which help people with health and wellbeing, managing bills and getting back into work, have been in Sheerness for the Swale Borough Council event on Thursday morning. Councillor Angela Harrison, deputy mayor of Swale, wants residents to know that "there is help support and guidance for you". Among those in attendance was Nichola Hermitage from Positively Connected Kent, which helps people manage energy costs and fuel debt.

items.title: Art of play in the age of AI
items.summary: As kids, we spent hours tinkering and building and just messing with things. As an adult, I could watch my own young kiddos figure out how certain shapes and movement work all day. Through that play, we improved our problem-solving and language skills, and it’s probably not a stretch to say it was good for our early engineering skills. In this era of development now, we’re starting to get a taste of that again. We’re experimenting more, and taking in more changes, because it’s all new! For the last four years at GitHub Universe, we’ve had hackable conference badges.

items.title: ‘Werwulf’: 5 Things to Know About Robert Eggers’ Medieval Horror Movie
items.summary: From witches to mermaids and even mustachioed vampires, New England filmmaker Robert Eggers has been stealthily setting up his own little monsterverse over the course of the past decade. That’s why it’s no surprise that the director’s latest release is set to be a lore-accurate reimagining of my personal favorite creature of ancient legend, the fearsome Werwulf. Though the film is set to release in less than a month, Egger’s disturbing period piece still remains just as enigmatic as it was when the first trailer dropped about five months ago.

items.title: The Illustrated Version of “Alice’s Restaurant”: Watch Arlo Guthrie’s Thanksgiving Counterculture Classic
items.summary: Alice’s Restaurant. It’s now a Thanksgiving classic, and something of a tradition around here. Recorded in 1967, the 18+ minute counterculture song recounts Arlo Guthrie’s real encounter with the law, starting on Thanksgiving Day 1965. As the long song unfolds, we hear all about how a hippie-bating police officer, by the name of William “Obie” Obanhein, arrested Arlo for littering. (Cultural footnote: Obie previously posed for several Norman Rockwell paintings, including the well-known painting, “The Runaway,” that graced a 1958 cover of The Saturday Evening Post.)

items.title: Mike Flanagan Gives an Update on ‘Carrie’ Season 2
items.summary: Even before Mike Flanagan’s Carrie series premiered on Prime Video, he was teasing a three-season arc for the show. But as it turns out, in Flanagan’s spin on the tale, Carrie survives âand the streamer soon confirmed her story would continue in a second season. However, in a new interview with the Hollywood Reporter, he says he “hoped” more than knew for certain that he’d get to do more.

items.title: Macdonald Book Shop in Estes Park, Colorado
items.summary: At Macdonald Book Shop, a cozy and beloved store in the Colorado mountain town of Estes Park, selling books began as a side hustle. J. Edward Macdonald bought a small log cabin in Estes Park in 1908 and opened a hardware and general store next door — with one corner full of books for sale. When he retired, his wife Jessica turned the parlor of their home into a proper bookstore, also selling magazines, stationery, and school supplies. That was 1928. Books have been the focus ever since. Over the decades, the shop expanded to claim more of the original house.

items.title: How iFood scales coding agents across 15,000 repositories
items.summary: The Remote Agents Platform turned engineering tasks into API calls: teams delegate the work, execution takes place in a remote sandbox, and the result comes back as a merge request. items.title: Blade Runner 2099 Proves The Saga Does One Thing Better Than Any Other Sci-Fi Franchise
items.summary: Continuing the legacy of two of the greatest sci-fi movies ever made is a big enough challenge. Doing so on the small screen adds an extra element of difficulty. Incredibly, "Blade Runner 2099" has overcome the odds to deliver yet another intoxicating excursion into the techno-industrial urban decay-scape so magically realized back in 1982's "Blade Runner" and so faithfully recreated in 2017's "Blade Runner 2049." As such, the Blade Runner franchise is now surely the most consistent on-screen sci-fi saga ever made.

items.title: Free Fall
items.summary: In contemplating the theory of general relativity, Albert Einstein imagined a falling lift in which people are performing experiments: One of the observers takes a handkerchief and a watch from his pocket and drops them. What happens to these two bodies? … or the outside observer they are both falling with the same acceleration. But so is the lift, with its walls, ceiling, and floor. Therefore: the distance between the two bodies and the floor will not change. This notion of the equivalence between gravity and acceleration, which he called “the happiest thought of my life,” came to Einstein in 1907.

items.title: Mpox cases are on the rise again in Brazil – just as an antiviral drug fails in trials
items.summary: The city of Rio de Janeiro has reported 180 confirmed cases of mpox, an infectious disease caused by the monkeypox virus, MPXV, from Oct. 1 through Nov. 24, 2026. Skin lesions are the most common sign of the disease. They can also appear in the mouth, on the genitals or in the anal region. Other symptoms include fever, swollen glands, headache, body aches, chills and weakness. items.title: GPT-6 models demonstrate intrinsic protein-design capabilities
items.summary: Our GPT‑6 family of models can design new protein shapes and the sequence of their chemical building blocks using only reasoning and code, without calling specialized biology models to generate those designs. An internal research model matched or outperformed specialized models on many protein design tasks. Researchers could also guide designs by prompting the model on where a protein should attach and what shape it should take. In lab tests with Onava, proteins based on GPT‑6.2’s designs showed evidence of binding, or attachment, across five targets.

items.title: ICAO Hosts Air Transport Conference, Elects New Council Members
items.summary: Last week, ICAO Headquarters in Montréal hosted the Seventh Worldwide Air Transport Conference, where Member States and industry stakeholders gathered to set global policy priorities on aviation economic regulation, infrastructure financing, resilience, consumer protection and sustainable growth. They discussed high-level topics in commercial aviation: modernizing economic and legal frameworks, investing in infrastructure and skilled workforces, and ensuring that innovation keeps pace with rapidly changing technologies and global demands.

items.summary: The Trump administration on Wednesday proposed a 10% tariff on finished aircraft imported from Brazil, potentially affecting business and commercial aircraft manufacturer Embraer. items.title: 6 Fantasy Books That Tried to Be Harry Potter

items.title: Keeping the great Arizona outdoors safe for pets
items.summary: Spending time outdoors is part of everyday life when you live in Arizona, especially in the fall and winter when temperatures hit near-perfect. Those outdoor adventures – a morning walk around the neighborhood, an afternoon hanging out in the backyard or an adventure on a local trail – are great for humans, and even better for pups. But the desert environment also comes with a few hazards that pet owners should understand before letting their furry friends explore. Arizona Humane Society’s Kelsey Dickerson has some advice for identifying outdoor risks and making a few adjustments around the home to help protect our four-legged family members.

items.title: This smart ring tracks your sleep and becomes your AI note-taker when you’re awake
items.summary: Most smart rings are basically a glorified diary strapped to your finger. They sit there, log your heart rate and your sleep stages, and wait until morning to hand you a report card on a night you already lived through. Oura does it, Ultrahuman does it, RingConn does it, and they all do it well. Their main job is quietly collecting data, while giving you few ways to interact with the rings themselves. items.title: How Hidden Gem ‘Door III’ Helped Shape Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s Signature J-Horror Style
items.summary: The term “ J-Horror ” seems pretty straightforward, but as it turns out, it doesn’t just mean “ Japanese horror ”. Or rather, it’s not a catch-all for every offering of Japanese horror—it better describes a particular movement and style. However, regardless of where you land on this topic, there is no argument that Kiyoshi Kurosawa is a key figure in J-Horror. Well before making waves with Pulse (2001), Kurosawa had already established himself in Japanese horror. These productions, all of which predate his career benchmark Cure (1997), go overlooked by the masses, but it’s his film Door III (1996) that helped shape what we now know as Kurosawa’s signature style.

items.title: 30+ editor-approved travel gifts for 2026
items.summary: Travel is the daily gift of life, but that doesn’t mean travel can’t suck the life out of you, even if you’re not going far. According to a study by the Institute of Environmental Science and Technology at the Autonomous University of Barcelona and McGill University, people travel an average of 78 minutes per day, regardless of mode of transport or distance covered. That means there’s a possibility of adventure in every bike ride, at each bus stop, and even while waiting in the airport security line.

items.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
items.summary: The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this "smoke taint" adversely affected not only local wine production, but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant. That's why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews.

items.title: NATO Deploys E-3A AWACS to Poland as Fleet Readiness Concerns Grow
items.summary: BRUSSELS- NATO has authorized the forward deployment of a Boeing E-3A Sentry Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft to Poland following an incident involving three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles that landed on Polish territory. The deployment highlights the importance of airborne surveillance along NATO’s eastern flank. However, publicly available flight-tracking data also raises questions about the availability of the alliance’s ageing fleet of 14 E-3A aircraft.

items.title: On a Ranch in Wyoming, a Stressed-Out Editor Gets in Sync With a Lazy Horse
items.summary: I used to avoid horses the same way I’d avoid palm readers. While my friends chased $5 readings in Downtown Manhattan, I preferred to keep the velvet curtain closed. I was convinced that once a fortune teller held my hands in hers, she would trace a life line abruptly cut short or reveal a heart line splintered beyond repair. So I’d sit on the stoop, hands safely secured in the pockets of my jacket. Horses and psychics, I believed, shared the same dark, all-knowing eyes. The first time I rode a horse was 10 years ago in Costa Rica, my body clenched for the entirety of the 20-minute sunset beach stroll.

items.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
items.summary: Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China's Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that's vital to the story of how our genus, Homo, took over the world. The chemical makeup of the teeth's enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we'd previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in.

items.summary: As dawn broke one recent morning over camp, we got one of our first full views of the peak of Mount Kilimanjaro, normally hidden behind clouds. items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have released Shirudo, an open-source Linux runtime for defending live systems. Teams get time to test and ship the real patch. The engineering came from Isovalent at Cisco, the team behind Cilium and Tetragon. TL;DR Size: Software runtime, not a model. Code is pre-release. items.title: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?

But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math.

items.title: ByteDance Researchers Open-Sources Laminar, an Async Reinforcement Learning RL Post-Training Framework
items.summary: Researchers from The University of Hong Kong and ByteDance Seed have open-sourced Laminar. Laminar is an reinforcement learning RL post-training framework for LLMs and long-horizon agents. The core idea is simple: stop forcing every trajectory and every GPU to wait for the slowest one. For teams training coding agents with long, skewed rollouts, that is where most GPU time goes. TL;DR What: A framework. Tested on Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct (30.5B total, 3.3B active) and Qwen2.5 at 7B, 32B and 72B.

items.title: Treasury CIO Is Vibe Coding a ‘Civilization’ Clone During Treasury Department Hack
items.summary: As the Treasury Department dealt with the fallout of a hack that took down some of its services, its Chief Information Officer was pushing updates to Legatum, his vibe coded Civilization clone. Sam Corcos is the cofounder of the A16z-backed glucose monitoring health startup called Levels; he became the Treasury Department’s Chief Information Officer as a DOGE hire near the beginning of Trump’s second term, and has been a leading AI evangelist within the administration since.

items.title: “I’m not going to remove the repository”
items.summary: There is a hacking tool called ARTEX that is causing havoc around the world. It lets a hacker plug in their LLM of choice, and ARTEX will then spin up a bunch of AI subagents focused on different aspects of hacking, such as scoping out a target or stealing data. This tool can complete an entire hack of a target in just a few hours. The original author of ARTEX took down the tool in October after it became clear that bad people were using it. But, as I write below, ARTEX is free. Several people are still distributing it on GitHub.
